bull.b: The financing arrangements provide access to additional capital over several years, improving Skye’s ability to fund operations and transactions. Although potentially dilutive, staged access and ownership limits may support funding continuity.

Combining with Redx would add a focused fibrosis pipeline and substantial committed funding, including support for a Phase 2 Crohn’s disease trial. This could diversify Skye’s platform and extend its development runway.

Very low absolute debt limits interest and refinancing obligations compared with a heavily leveraged biotech. This preserves flexibility to direct available capital toward research, clinical development and strategic transactions.

bear.b: Without commercial revenue, Skye remains dependent on financing and clinical progress to build value. Losses have widened materially, indicating that operating costs are increasing faster than any developing revenue base.

Persistent cash outflows require recurring external funding and leave limited capacity to absorb clinical setbacks or delays. Because free cash flow broadly tracks net loss, the reported losses are translating into substantial real cash consumption.

bear.t: Negative Equity and Nasdaq Compliance Risk
bear.b: Negative equity weakens the company’s capital cushion and creates an ongoing requirement to raise funds or restructure. Failure to restore compliance could disrupt strategic plans, increase financing pressure and threaten continued exchange listing.
